content.latin: Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
content.english: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.

content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
content.english: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

content.latin: Ant. Intercéde pro nobis.
content.english: Ant. Mother of God, pray for us.

segments.t: Ant.
Intercéde pro nobis.

content.latin: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius (genuflectitur) veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

segments.t: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius
(genuflectitur)
veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.

content.latin: Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
content.english: Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.

content.latin: Ant. Intercéde pro nobis.

content.latin: Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
content.english: Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

content.latin: Psalmus 13 [1]
content.english: Psalm 13 [1]

segments.t: Psalmus 13

content.latin: 13:1 Dixit insípiens in corde suo: * non est Deus.
content.english: 13:1 The fool hath said in his heart: * there is no God.

segments.t: Dixit insípiens in corde suo: * non est Deus.

content.latin: 13:1 Corrúpti sunt, et abominábiles facti sunt in stúdiis suis: * non est qui fáciat bonum, non est usque ad unum.
content.english: 13:1 They are corrupt, and are become abominable in their ways: * there is none that doth good, no not one.

segments.t: Corrúpti sunt, et abominábiles facti sunt in stúdiis suis: * non est qui fáciat bonum, non est usque ad unum.

content.latin: 13:2 Dóminus de cælo prospéxit super fílios hóminum, * ut vídeat si est intéllegens, aut requírens Deum.
content.english: 13:2 The Lord hath looked down from heaven upon the children of men, * to see if there be any that understand and seek God.

segments.t: Dóminus de cælo prospéxit super fílios hóminum, * ut vídeat si est intéllegens, aut requírens Deum.

content.latin: 13:3 Omnes declinavérunt, simul inútiles facti sunt: * non est qui fáciat bonum, non est usque ad unum.
content.english: 13:3 They are all gone aside, they are become unprofitable together: * there is none that doth good: no not one.

segments.t: Omnes declinavérunt, simul inútiles facti sunt: * non est qui fáciat bonum, non est usque ad unum.

content.latin: 13:3 Sepúlcrum patens est guttur eórum: linguis suis dolóse agébant * venénum áspidum sub lábiis eórum.
content.english: 13:3 Their throat is an open sepulchre; with their tongues they acted deceitfully: * the poison of asps is under their lips.

segments.t: Sepúlcrum patens est guttur eórum: linguis suis dolóse agébant * venénum áspidum sub lábiis eórum.

content.latin: 13:3 Quorum os maledictióne et amaritúdine plenum est: * velóces pedes eórum ad effundéndum sánguinem.
content.english: 13:3 Their mouth is full of cursing and bitterness; * their feet are swift to shed blood.

segments.t: Quorum os maledictióne et amaritúdine plenum est: * velóces pedes eórum ad effundéndum sánguinem.

content.latin: 13:3 Contrítio et infelícitas in viis eórum, et viam pacis non cognovérunt: * non est timor Dei ante óculos eórum.
content.english: 13:3 Destruction and unhappiness in their ways; and the way of peace they have not known: * there is no fear of God before their eyes.

segments.t: Contrítio et infelícitas in viis eórum, et viam pacis non cognovérunt: * non est timor Dei ante óculos eórum.

content.latin: 13:4 Nonne cognóscent omnes qui operántur iniquitátem, * qui dévorant plebem meam sicut escam panis?
content.english: 13:4 Shall not all they know that work iniquity, * who devour my people as they eat bread?

segments.t: Nonne cognóscent omnes qui operántur iniquitátem, * qui dévorant plebem meam sicut escam panis?

content.latin: 13:5 Dóminum non invocavérunt, * illic trepidavérunt timóre, ubi non erat timor.
content.english: 13:5 They have not called upon the Lord: * there have they trembled for fear, where there was no fear.

segments.t: Dóminum non invocavérunt, * illic trepidavérunt timóre, ubi non erat timor.

content.latin: 13:6 Quóniam Dóminus in generatióne iusta est, consílium ínopis confudístis: * quóniam Dóminus spes eius est.
content.english: 13:6 For the Lord is in the just generation: you have confounded the counsel of the poor man; * but the Lord is his hope.

segments.t: Quóniam Dóminus in generatióne iusta est, consílium ínopis confudístis: * quóniam Dóminus spes eius est.

content.latin: 13:7 Quis dabit ex Sion salutáre Israël? * cum avérterit Dóminus captivitátem plebis suæ, exsultábit Iacob, et lætábitur Israël.
content.english: 13:7 Who shall give out of Sion the salvation of Israel? * when the Lord shall have turned away the captivity of his people, Jacob shall rejoice, and Israel shall be glad.

segments.t: Quis dabit ex Sion salutáre Israël? * cum avérterit Dóminus captivitátem plebis suæ, exsultábit Iacob, et lætábitur Israël.

segments.t: Psalmus 14

content.latin: 14:1 Dómine, quis habitábit in tabernáculo tuo? * aut quis requiéscet in monte sancto tuo?
content.english: 14:1 Lord, who shall dwell in thy tabernacle? * or who shall rest in thy holy hill?

segments.t: Dómine, quis habitábit in tabernáculo tuo? * aut quis requiéscet in monte sancto tuo?

content.latin: 14:2 Qui ingréditur sine mácula, * et operátur iustítiam:
content.english: 14:2 He that walketh without blemish, * and worketh justice:

segments.t: Qui ingréditur sine mácula, * et operátur iustítiam:

content.latin: 14:3 Qui lóquitur veritátem in corde suo, * qui non egit dolum in lingua sua:
content.english: 14:3 He that speaketh truth in his heart, * who hath not used deceit in his tongue:

segments.t: Qui lóquitur veritátem in corde suo, * qui non egit dolum in lingua sua:

content.latin: 14:3 Nec fecit próximo suo malum, * et oppróbrium non accépit advérsus próximos suos.
content.english: 14:3 Nor hath done evil to his neighbour: * nor taken up a reproach against his neighbours.

segments.t: Nec fecit próximo suo malum, * et oppróbrium non accépit advérsus próximos suos.

content.latin: 14:4 Ad níhilum dedúctus est in conspéctu eius malígnus: * timéntes autem Dóminum gloríficat:
content.english: 14:4 In his sight the malignant is brought to nothing: * but he glorifieth them that fear the Lord:

segments.t: Ad níhilum dedúctus est in conspéctu eius malígnus: * timéntes autem Dóminum gloríficat:

content.latin: 14:4 Qui iurat próximo suo, et non décipit, * qui pecúniam suam non dedit ad usúram, et múnera super innocéntem non accépit.
content.english: 14:4 He that sweareth to his neighbour, and deceiveth not; * He that hath not put out his money to usury, nor taken bribes against the innocent:

segments.t: Qui iurat próximo suo, et non décipit, * qui pecúniam suam non dedit ad usúram, et múnera super innocéntem non accépit.

content.latin: 14:5 Qui facit hæc: * non movébitur in ætérnum.
content.english: 14:5 He that doth these things, * shall not be moved for ever.

segments.t: Qui facit hæc: * non movébitur in ætérnum.

content.english: Ant. O Lord, incline * thy ear to me, and hear my voice, my Lord.

content.latin: Psalmus 16 [3]
content.english: Psalm 16 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 16

content.latin: 16:1 Exáudi, Dómine, iustítiam meam: * inténde deprecatiónem meam.
content.english: 16:1 Hear, O Lord, my justice: * attend to my supplication.

segments.t: Exáudi, Dómine, iustítiam meam: * inténde deprecatiónem meam.

content.latin: 16:1 Áuribus pércipe oratiónem meam, * non in lábiis dolósis.
content.english: 16:1 Give ear unto my prayer, * which proceedeth not from deceitful lips.

segments.t: Áuribus pércipe oratiónem meam, * non in lábiis dolósis.

content.latin: 16:2 De vultu tuo iudícium meum pródeat: * óculi tui vídeant æquitátes.
content.english: 16:2 Let my judgment come forth from thy countenance: * let thy eyes behold the things that are equitable.

segments.t: De vultu tuo iudícium meum pródeat: * óculi tui vídeant æquitátes.

content.latin: 16:3 Probásti cor meum, et visitásti nocte: * igne me examinásti, et non est invénta in me iníquitas.
content.english: 16:3 Thou hast proved my heart, and visited it by night, * thou hast tried me by fire: and iniquity hath not been found in me.

segments.t: Probásti cor meum, et visitásti nocte: * igne me examinásti, et non est invénta in me iníquitas.

content.latin: 16:4 Ut non loquátur os meum ópera hóminum: * propter verba labiórum tuórum ego custodívi vias duras.
content.english: 16:4 That my mouth may not speak the works of men: * for the sake of the words of thy lips, I have kept hard ways.

segments.t: Ut non loquátur os meum ópera hóminum: * propter verba labiórum tuórum ego custodívi vias duras.

content.latin: 16:5 Pérfice gressus meos in sémitis tuis: * ut non moveántur vestígia mea.
content.english: 16:5 Perfect thou my goings in thy paths: * that my footsteps be not moved.

segments.t: Pérfice gressus meos in sémitis tuis: * ut non moveántur vestígia mea.

content.latin: 16:6 Ego clamávi, quóniam exaudísti me, Deus: * inclína aurem tuam mihi, et exáudi verba mea.
content.english: 16:6 I have cried to thee, for thou, O God, hast heard me: * O incline thy ear unto me, and hear my words.

segments.t: Ego clamávi, quóniam exaudísti me, Deus: * inclína aurem tuam mihi, et exáudi verba mea.

content.latin: 16:7 Mirífica misericórdias tuas, * qui salvos facis sperántes in te.
content.english: 16:7 Shew forth thy wonderful mercies; * thou who savest them that trust in thee.

segments.t: Mirífica misericórdias tuas, * qui salvos facis sperántes in te.

content.latin: 16:8 A resisténtibus déxteræ tuæ custódi me, * ut pupíllam óculi.
content.english: 16:8 From them that resist thy right hand keep me, * as the apple of thy eye.

segments.t: A resisténtibus déxteræ tuæ custódi me, * ut pupíllam óculi.

content.latin: 16:8 Sub umbra alárum tuárum prótege me: * a fácie impiórum qui me afflixérunt.
content.english: 16:8 Protect me under the shadow of thy wings: * from the face of the wicked who have afflicted me.

segments.t: Sub umbra alárum tuárum prótege me: * a fácie impiórum qui me afflixérunt.

content.latin: 16:9 Inimíci mei ánimam meam circumdedérunt, ádipem suum conclusérunt: * os eórum locútum est supérbiam.
content.english: 16:9 My enemies have surrounded my soul: They have shut up their fat: * their mouth hath spoken proudly.

segments.t: Inimíci mei ánimam meam circumdedérunt, ádipem suum conclusérunt: * os eórum locútum est supérbiam.

content.latin: 16:11 Proiciéntes me nunc circumdedérunt me: * óculos suos statuérunt declináre in terram.
content.english: 16:11 They have cast me forth, and now they have surrounded me: * they have set their eyes bowing down to the earth.

segments.t: Proiciéntes me nunc circumdedérunt me: * óculos suos statuérunt declináre in terram.

content.latin: 16:12 Suscepérunt me sicut leo parátus ad prædam: * et sicut cátulus leónis hábitans in ábditis.
content.english: 16:12 They have taken me, as a lion prepared for the prey; * and as a young lion dwelling in secret places.

segments.t: Suscepérunt me sicut leo parátus ad prædam: * et sicut cátulus leónis hábitans in ábditis.

content.latin: 16:13 Exsúrge, Dómine, prǽveni eum, et supplánta eum: * éripe ánimam meam ab ímpio, frámeam tuam ab inimícis manus tuæ.
content.english: 16:13 Arise, O Lord, disappoint him and supplant him; * deliver my soul from the wicked one; thy sword from the enemies of thy hand.

segments.t: Exsúrge, Dómine, prǽveni eum, et supplánta eum: * éripe ánimam meam ab ímpio, frámeam tuam ab inimícis manus tuæ.

content.latin: 16:14 Dómine, a paucis de terra dívide eos in vita eórum: * de abscónditis tuis adimplétus est venter eórum.
content.english: 16:14 O Lord, divide them from the few of the earth in their life: * their belly is filled from thy hidden stores.

segments.t: Dómine, a paucis de terra dívide eos in vita eórum: * de abscónditis tuis adimplétus est venter eórum.

content.latin: 16:14 Saturáti sunt fíliis: * et dimisérunt relíquias suas párvulis suis.
content.english: 16:14 They are full of children: * and they have left to their little ones the rest of their substance.

segments.t: Saturáti sunt fíliis: * et dimisérunt relíquias suas párvulis suis.

content.latin: 16:15 Ego autem in iustítia apparébo conspéctui tuo: * satiábor cum apparúerit glória tua.
content.english: 16:15 But as for me, I will appear before thy sight in justice: * I shall be satisfied when thy glory shall appear.

segments.t: Ego autem in iustítia apparébo conspéctui tuo: * satiábor cum apparúerit glória tua.

content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Inclína, Dómine, aurem tuam mihi, et exáudi verba mea.
content.english: Ant. O Lord, incline thy ear to me, and hear my voice, my Lord.

segments.t: Ant.
Inclína, Dómine, aurem tuam mihi, et exáudi verba mea.

content.latin: ℣. Mirífica Dómine misericórdias tuas.
content.english: ℣. Show forth thy wonderful mercies.

segments.t: Mirífica Dómine misericórdias tuas.

content.latin: ℟. Qui salvos facis sperántes in te.
content.english: ℟. Thou who savest them that trust in thee.

segments.t: Qui salvos facis sperántes in te.

content.latin: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

segments.t: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

segments.t: Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

segments.t: Sed líbera nos a malo.

content.latin: Absolutio. Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Absolution. O Lord Jesus Christ, graciously hear the prayers of Thy servants, and have mercy upon us, Who livest and reignest with the Father, and the Holy Ghost, ever world without end.

segments.t: Absolutio.
Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.

content.english: Lesson from the book of Proverbs

content.latin: 12 Ego sapiéntia hábito in consílio et erudítis intérsum cogitatiónibus.
content.english: 12 I wisdom dwell in counsel, and am present in learned thoughts.

segments.t: Ego sapiéntia hábito in consílio et erudítis intérsum cogitatiónibus.

content.latin: 13 Timor Dómini odit malum: arrogántiam, et supérbiam, et viam pravam, et os bilíngue detéstor.
content.english: 13 The fear of the Lord hateth evil: I hate arrogance, and pride, and every wicked way, and a mouth with a double tongue.

segments.t: Timor Dómini odit malum: arrogántiam, et supérbiam, et viam pravam, et os bilíngue detéstor.

content.latin: 14 Meum est consílium et ǽquitas, mea est prudéntia, mea est fortitúdo.
content.english: 14 Counsel and equity is mine, prudence is mine, strength is mine.

segments.t: Meum est consílium et ǽquitas, mea est prudéntia, mea est fortitúdo.

content.latin: 15 Per me reges regnant, et legum conditóres iusta decérnunt;
content.english: 15 By me kings reign, and lawgivers decree just things,

segments.t: Per me reges regnant, et legum conditóres iusta decérnunt;

content.latin: 16 Per me príncipes ímperant, et poténtes decérnunt iustítiam.
content.english: 16 By me princes rule, and the mighty decree justice.

segments.t: Per me príncipes ímperant, et poténtes decérnunt iustítiam.

content.latin: 17 Ego diligéntes me díligo; et qui mane vígilant ad me, invénient me.
content.english: 17 I love them that love me: and they that in the morning early watch for me, shall find me.

segments.t: Ego diligéntes me díligo; et qui mane vígilant ad me, invénient me.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Sancta et immaculáta virgínitas, quibus te láudibus éfferam, néscio:
content.english: ℟. O how holy and how spotless is thy virginity; I am too dull to praise thee:

segments.t: Sancta et immaculáta virgínitas, quibus te láudibus éfferam, néscio:

content.latin: * Quia quem cæli cápere non póterant, tuo grémio contulísti.
content.english: * For thou hast borne in thy breast Him Whom the heavens cannot contain.

content.latin: ℣. Benedícta tu in muliéribus, et benedíctus fructus ventris tui.
content.english: ℣. Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb.

segments.t: Benedícta tu in muliéribus, et benedíctus fructus ventris tui.

content.latin: ℟. Quia quem cæli cápere non póterant, tuo grémio contulisti.
content.english: ℟. For thou hast borne in thy breast Him Whom the heavens cannot contain.

segments.t: Quia quem cæli cápere non póterant, tuo grémio contulisti.

content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

content.english: Benediction. May the Son, the Sole-begotten, mercifully bless and keep us.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adiuváre dignétur.

content.latin: 18 Mecum sunt divítiæ et glória, opes supérbæ et iustítia.
content.english: 18 With me are riches and glory, glorious riches and justice.

segments.t: Mecum sunt divítiæ et glória, opes supérbæ et iustítia.

content.latin: 19 Mélior est enim fructus meus auro et lápide pretióso, et genímina mea argénto elécto.
content.english: 19 For my fruit is better than gold and the precious stone, and my blossoms than choice silver.

segments.t: Mélior est enim fructus meus auro et lápide pretióso, et genímina mea argénto elécto.

content.latin: 20 In viis iustítiæ ámbulo, in médio semitárum iudícii,
content.english: 20 I walk in the way of justice, in the midst of the paths of judgment,

segments.t: In viis iustítiæ ámbulo, in médio semitárum iudícii,

content.latin: 21 Ut ditem diligéntes me et thesáuros eórum répleam.
content.english: 21 That I may enrich them that love me, and may fill their treasures.

segments.t: Ut ditem diligéntes me et thesáuros eórum répleam.

content.latin: 22 Dóminus possidébit me in inítio viárum suárum, ántequam quidquam fáceret a princípio.
content.english: 22 The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his ways, before he made any thing from the beginning.

segments.t: Dóminus possidébit me in inítio viárum suárum, ántequam quidquam fáceret a princípio.

content.latin: 23 Ab ætérno ordináta sum et ex antíquis, ántequam terra fíeret.
content.english: 23 I was set up from eternity, and of old before the earth was made.

segments.t: Ab ætérno ordináta sum et ex antíquis, ántequam terra fíeret.

content.latin: 24 Nondum erant abýssi, et ego iam concépta eram;
content.english: 24 The depths were not as yet, and I was already conceived. neither had the fountains of waters as yet sprung out:

segments.t: Nondum erant abýssi, et ego iam concépta eram;

content.latin: 25 Necdum fontes aquárum erúperant, necdum montes gravi mole constíterant; ante colles ego parturiébar.
content.english: 25 The mountains with their huge bulk had not as yet been established: before the hills I was brought forth:

segments.t: Necdum fontes aquárum erúperant, necdum montes gravi mole constíterant; ante colles ego parturiébar.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Congratulámini mihi, omnes qui dilígitis Dóminum: quia cum essem párvula, plácui Altíssimo,
content.english: ℟. Rejoice with me, all ye that love the Lord, for while I was yet a little one, I pleased the Most High.

segments.t: Congratulámini mihi, omnes qui dilígitis Dóminum: quia cum essem párvula, plácui Altíssimo,

content.latin: * Et de meis viscéribus génui Deum et hóminem.
content.english: * And I have brought forth from my bowels God and man.

content.latin: ℣. Beátam me dicent omnes generatiónes, quia ancíllam húmilem respéxit Deus.
content.english: ℣. All generations shall call me blessed, since the Lord hath regarded the lowliness of his handmaiden.

segments.t: Beátam me dicent omnes generatiónes, quia ancíllam húmilem respéxit Deus.

content.latin: ℟. Et de meis viscéribus génui Deum et hóminem.
content.english: ℟. And I have brought forth from my bowels God and man.

segments.t: Et de meis viscéribus génui Deum et hóminem.

content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.
content.english: Benediction. May the grace of the Holy Spirit enlighten all our hearts and minds.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: 34 Beátus homo qui audit me, et qui vígilat ad fores meas cotídie, et obsérvat ad postes óstii mei.
content.english: 34 Blessed is the man that heareth me, and that watcheth daily at my gates, and waiteth at the posts of my doors.

segments.t: Beátus homo qui audit me, et qui vígilat ad fores meas cotídie, et obsérvat ad postes óstii mei.

content.latin: 35 Qui me invénerit, invéniet vitam, et háuriet salútem a Dómino;
content.english: 35 He that shall find me, shall find life, and shall have salvation from the Lord:

segments.t: Qui me invénerit, invéniet vitam, et háuriet salútem a Dómino;

content.latin: 36 Qui autem in me peccáverit, lædet ánimam suam. Omnes, qui me odérunt, díligunt mortem.
content.english: 36 But he that shall sin against me, shall hurt his own soul. All that hate me love death.

segments.t: Qui autem in me peccáverit, lædet ánimam suam. Omnes, qui me odérunt, díligunt mortem.

content.latin: 1 Sapiéntia ædificávit sibi domum, excídit colúmnas septem.
content.english: 1 Wisdom hath built herself a house, she hath hewn out her seven pillars.

segments.t: Sapiéntia ædificávit sibi domum, excídit colúmnas septem.

content.latin: 2 Immolávit víctimas suas, míscuit vinum et propósuit mensam suam.
content.english: 2 She hath slain her victims, mingled her wine, and set forth her table.

segments.t: Immolávit víctimas suas, míscuit vinum et propósuit mensam suam.

content.latin: 3 Misit ancíllas suas ut vocárent ad arcem et ad mœ́nia civitátis:
content.english: 3 She hath sent her maids to invite to the tower, and to the walls of the city:

segments.t: Misit ancíllas suas ut vocárent ad arcem et ad mœ́nia civitátis:

content.latin: 4 Si quis est párvulus, véniat ad me. Et insipiéntibus locúta est:
content.english: 4 Whosoever is a little one, let him come to me. And to the unwise she said:

segments.t: Si quis est párvulus, véniat ad me. Et insipiéntibus locúta est:

content.latin: 5 Veníte, comédite panem meum, et bíbite vinum quod míscui vobis.
content.english: 5 Come, eat my bread, and drink the wine which I have mingled for you

segments.t: Veníte, comédite panem meum, et bíbite vinum quod míscui vobis.

content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.english: ℟. Blessed art thou, O Virgin Mary, who hast carried the Lord, the Maker of the world.

segments.t: Beáta es, Virgo María, quæ Dóminum portásti, Creatórem mundi:

content.latin: * Genuísti qui te fecit, et in ætérnum pérmanes Virgo.
content.english: * Thou hast borne Him Who created thee, and thou abidest a virgin for ever.

content.latin: Psalmus 17(2-16b) [4]

segments.t: Psalmus 17(2-16b)

content.latin: 17:2 Díligam te, Dómine, fortitúdo mea: * Dóminus firmaméntum meum, et refúgium meum, et liberátor meus.
content.english: 17:2 I will love thee, O Lord, my strength: * The Lord is my firmament, my refuge, and my deliverer.

segments.t: Díligam te, Dómine, fortitúdo mea: * Dóminus firmaméntum meum, et refúgium meum, et liberátor meus.

content.latin: 17:3 Deus meus adiútor meus, * et sperábo in eum.
content.english: 17:3 My God is my helper, * and in him will I put my trust.

segments.t: Deus meus adiútor meus, * et sperábo in eum.

content.latin: 17:3 Protéctor meus, et cornu salútis meæ, * et suscéptor meus.
content.english: 17:3 My protector, and the horn of my salvation, * and my support.

segments.t: Protéctor meus, et cornu salútis meæ, * et suscéptor meus.

content.latin: 17:4 Laudans invocábo Dóminum: * et ab inimícis meis salvus ero.
content.english: 17:4 Praising, I will call upon the Lord: * and I shall be saved from my enemies.

segments.t: Laudans invocábo Dóminum: * et ab inimícis meis salvus ero.

content.latin: 17:5 Circumdedérunt me dolóres mortis: * et torréntes iniquitátis conturbavérunt me.
content.english: 17:5 The sorrows of death surrounded me: * and the torrents of iniquity troubled me.

segments.t: Circumdedérunt me dolóres mortis: * et torréntes iniquitátis conturbavérunt me.

content.latin: 17:6 Dolóres inférni circumdedérunt me: * præoccupavérunt me láquei mortis.
content.english: 17:6 The sorrows of hell encompassed me: * and the snares of death prevented me.

segments.t: Dolóres inférni circumdedérunt me: * præoccupavérunt me láquei mortis.

content.latin: 17:7 In tribulatióne mea invocávi Dóminum, * et ad Deum meum clamávi.
content.english: 17:7 In my affliction I called upon the Lord, * and I cried to my God:

segments.t: In tribulatióne mea invocávi Dóminum, * et ad Deum meum clamávi.

content.latin: 17:7 Et exaudívit de templo sancto suo vocem meam: * et clamor meus in conspéctu eius, introívit in aures eius.
content.english: 17:7 And he heard my voice from his holy temple: * and my cry before him came into his ears.

segments.t: Et exaudívit de templo sancto suo vocem meam: * et clamor meus in conspéctu eius, introívit in aures eius.

content.latin: 17:8 Commóta est, et contrémuit terra: * fundaménta móntium conturbáta sunt, et commóta sunt, quóniam irátus est eis.
content.english: 17:8 The earth shook and trembled: * the foundations of the mountains were troubled and were moved, because he was angry with them.

segments.t: Commóta est, et contrémuit terra: * fundaménta móntium conturbáta sunt, et commóta sunt, quóniam irátus est eis.

content.latin: 17:9 Ascéndit fumus in ira eius: et ignis a fácie eius exársit: * carbónes succénsi sunt ab eo.
content.english: 17:9 There went up a smoke in his wrath: and a fire flamed from his face: * coals were kindled by it.

segments.t: Ascéndit fumus in ira eius: et ignis a fácie eius exársit: * carbónes succénsi sunt ab eo.

content.latin: 17:10 Inclinávit cælos, et descéndit: * et calígo sub pédibus eius.
content.english: 17:10 He bowed the heavens, and came down, * and darkness was under his feet.

segments.t: Inclinávit cælos, et descéndit: * et calígo sub pédibus eius.

content.latin: 17:11 Et ascéndit super Chérubim, et volávit: * volávit super pennas ventórum.
content.english: 17:11 And he ascended upon the cherubim, and he flew; * he flew upon the wings of the winds.

segments.t: Et ascéndit super Chérubim, et volávit: * volávit super pennas ventórum.

content.latin: 17:12 Et pósuit ténebras latíbulum suum, in circúitu eius tabernáculum eius: * tenebrósa aqua in núbibus áëris.
content.english: 17:12 And he made darkness his covert, his pavilion round about him: * dark waters in the clouds of the air.

segments.t: Et pósuit ténebras latíbulum suum, in circúitu eius tabernáculum eius: * tenebrósa aqua in núbibus áëris.

content.latin: 17:13 Præ fulgóre in conspéctu eius nubes transiérunt, * grando et carbónes ignis.
content.english: 17:13 At the brightness that was before him the clouds passed, * hail and coals of fire.

segments.t: Præ fulgóre in conspéctu eius nubes transiérunt, * grando et carbónes ignis.

content.latin: 17:14 Et intónuit de cælo Dóminus, et Altíssimus dedit vocem suam: * grando et carbónes ignis.
content.english: 17:14 And the Lord thundered from heaven, and the Highest gave his voice: * hail and coals of fire.

segments.t: Et intónuit de cælo Dóminus, et Altíssimus dedit vocem suam: * grando et carbónes ignis.

content.latin: 17:15 Et misit sagíttas suas, et dissipávit eos: * fúlgura multiplicávit, et conturbávit eos.
content.english: 17:15 And he sent forth his arrows, and he scattered them: * he multiplied lightnings, and troubled them.

segments.t: Et misit sagíttas suas, et dissipávit eos: * fúlgura multiplicávit, et conturbávit eos.

content.latin: 17:16 Et apparuérunt fontes aquárum, * et reveláta sunt fundaménta orbis terrárum:
content.english: 17:16 Then the fountains of waters appeared, * and the foundations of the world were discovered:

segments.t: Et apparuérunt fontes aquárum, * et reveláta sunt fundaménta orbis terrárum:

content.latin: 17:16 Ab increpatióne tua, Dómine, * ab inspiratióne spíritus iræ tuæ.
content.english: 17:16 At thy rebuke, O Lord, * at the blast of the spirit of thy wrath.

segments.t: Ab increpatióne tua, Dómine, * ab inspiratióne spíritus iræ tuæ.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.english: Ant. I will love thee, O Lord, who art my strength.

segments.t: Ant.
Díligam te, Dómine, virtus mea.

content.latin: 17:17 Misit de summo, et accépit me: * et assúmpsit me de aquis multis.
content.english: 17:17 He sent from on high, and took me: * and received me out of many waters.

segments.t: Misit de summo, et accépit me: * et assúmpsit me de aquis multis.

content.latin: 17:18 Erípuit me de inimícis meis fortíssimis, et ab his qui odérunt me: * quóniam confortáti sunt super me.
content.english: 17:18 He delivered me from my strongest enemies, and from them that hated me: * for they were too strong for me.

segments.t: Erípuit me de inimícis meis fortíssimis, et ab his qui odérunt me: * quóniam confortáti sunt super me.

content.latin: Dei Fílius non dívitem aut locuplétem áliquam féminam sibi matrem elégit, sed beátam Vírginem illam, cuius ánima virtútibus ornáta erat. Cum enim beáta María supra omnem humánam natúram castitátem serváret, proptérea Christum Dóminum in ventre concépit. Ad hanc ígitur sanctíssimam Vírginem et Dei Matrem accurréntes, eius patrocínii utilitátem assequámur. Itaque, quæcúmque estis vírgines, ad Matrem Dómini confúgite; illa enim pulchérrimam, pretiosíssimam et incorruptíbilem possessiónem, patrocínio suo, vobis conservábit.
content.english: That is wealth, not a woman of substance, but that blessed maiden whose soul was bright with grace. It was because Blessed Mary had preserved a superhuman chastity, that she conceived the Lord Jesus Christ in her womb. Let us then fly to the most holy maiden, who is Mother of God, that we may gain the help of her patronage. Yea, all ye that be virgins, whosoever ye be, run to the Mother of the Lord. She will keep for you by her protection your most beautiful, your most precious, and your most enduring possession.

content.latin: Magnum revéra miráculum, fratres dilectíssimi, fuit beáta semper Virgo María. Quid namque illa maius aut illústrius ullo umquam témpore invéntum est, seu aliquándo inveníri póterit? Hæc sola cælum ac terram amplitúdine superávit. Quidnam illa sánctius? Non Prophétæ, non Apóstoli, non Mártyres, non Patriárchæ, non Angeli, non Throni, non Dominatiónes, non Séraphim, non Chérubim; non deníque áliud quidpíam, inter creátas res visíbiles aut invisíbiles, maius aut excelléntius inveníri potest. Eádem ancílla Dei est et mater; eádem Virgo et Génetrix.
content.english: Dearly beloved brethren, the Blessed Virgin Mary was a great wonder. What thing greater or more famous than she, hath ever at any time been found, or can be found She alone is greater than heaven and earth. What thing holier than she hath been, or can be found? Neither Prophets, nor Apostles, nor Martyrs, nor Patriarchs, nor Angels, nor Thrones, nor Lordships, nor Seraphim, nor Cherubim, nor any other creature, visible or invisible, can be found that is greater or more excellent than she. She is at once the hand-maid and the parent of God, at once virgin and mother.

content.latin: Hæc eius mater est, qui a Patre ante omne princípium génitus fuit; quem Angeli et hómines agnóscunt Dóminum rerum ómnium. Visne cognóscere quanto Virgo hæc præstántior sit cæléstibus Poténtiis? Illæ cum timóre et tremóre assístunt, fáciem velántes suam: hæc humánum genus illi offert, quem génuit. Per hanc et peccatórum véniam conséquimur. Ave ígitur, mater, cælum, puélla, virgo, thronus. Ecclésiæ nostræ decus, glória et firmaméntum: assídue pro nobis precáre Iesum, Fílium tuum et Dóminum nostrum, ut per te misericórdiam inveníre in die iudícii, et quæ repósita sunt iis qui díligunt Deum bona cónsequi possímus, grátia et benignitáte Dómini nostri Iesu Christi: cum quo Patri simul et Sancto Spirítui glória, et honor, et impérium, nunc et semper in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: She is the Mother of him who was begotten of the Father before all ages, and who is acknowledged by Angels and men to be Lord of all. Wouldst thou know how much nobler is this virgin than any of the heavenly powers. They stand before Him with fear and trembling, veiling their faces with their wings, but she offereth humanity to Him to Whom she gave birth. Through her we obtain the remission of sins. Hail, then, O Mother! heaven! damsel! maiden! throne! adornment, and glory, and foundation, of our Church! cease not to pray for us to thy Son and our Lord Jesus Christ that through thee we may find mercy in the day of judgment, and may be able to obtain those good things which God hath prepared for them that love Him, by the grace and goodness of our Lord Jesus Christ to Whom, with the Father, and the Holy Ghost, be ascribed all glory, and honour, and power, now, and for ever and ever. Amen.

content.latin: Lib 4. cap. 49. in Luc. 11.
content.english: Lib 4 Cap 49 in Luke 11

content.latin: Magnæ devotiónis et fídei hæc múlier osténditur, quæ, scribis et pharisǽis Dóminum tentántibus simul et blasphemántibus, tanta eius incarnatiónem præ ómnibus sinceritáte cognóscit, tanta fidúcia confitétur, ut et præséntium prócerum calúmniam, et futurórum confúndat hæreticórum perfídiam. Nam, sicut tunc Iudǽi, Sancti Spíritus ópera blasphemándo, verum consubstantialémque Patri Dei Fílium negábant; sic hærétici póstea, negándo Maríam semper Vírginem, Sancti Spíritus operánte virtúte, nascitúro cum humánis membris Unigénito Dei, carnis suæ matériam ministrásse, verum consubstantialémque matri Fílium hóminis fatéri non debére dixérunt.
content.english: It is plain that this was a woman of great earnestness and faith. The Scribes and Pharisees were at once tempting and blaspheming the Lord, but this woman so clearly grasped His Incarnation, and so bravely confessed the same, that she confounded both the lies of the great men who were present, and the faithlessness of the heretics who were yet to come. Even as the Jews then, blaspheming the works of the Holy Ghost, denied the very Son of God Who is of one substance with the Father, so afterwards did the heretics, by denying that Mary always a Virgin did, under the operation of the Holy Ghost, supply flesh to the Only begotten One of God, when He was about being born in an human Body, even so, I say, did the heretics deny that the Son of Man should be called a true Son, Who is of one substance with His Mother.

content.latin: Sed, si caro Verbi Dei secúndum carnem nascéntis a carne Vírginis matris pronuntiátur extránea, sine causa venter qui eam portásset, úbera quæ lactássent, beatificántur. Dicit autem Apóstolus: Quia misit Deus Fílium suum, factum ex mulíere, factum sub lege. Neque audiéndi sunt, qui legéndum putant: Natum ex mulíere, factum sub lege, sed Factum ex mulíere; quia concéptus ex útero virgináli, carnem non de níhilo, non aliúnde, sed matérna traxit ex carne. Alióquin nec vere Fílius hóminis dicerétur, qui oríginem non habéret ex hómine. Et nos ígitur, his contra Eutychen dictis, extollámus vocem cum Ecclésia cathólica, cuius hæc múlier typum gessit, extollámus et mentem de médio turbárum, dicamúsque Salvatóri: Beátus venter qui te portávit, et úbera quæ suxísti. Vere enim beáta parens, quæ, sicut quidam ait, Eníxa est puérpera Regem, qui cælum terrámque tenet per sǽcula.
content.english: If we shall say that the Flesh, Wherewith the Son of God was born in the flesh, was something outside of the flesh of the Virgin His Mother, without reason should we bless the womb that bore Him, and the paps which He hath sucked. But the Apostle saith: “God sent forth His Son, made of a woman, made under the law”, Gal. iv. 4, and they are not to be listened to who read this passage: “Born of a woman, made under the law.” He was made of a woman, for He was conceived in a virgin's womb, and took His Flesh, not from nothing, not from elsewhere, but from the flesh of His Mother. Otherwise, and if He had not been sprung of a woman, He could not with truth be called the Son of man. Let us therefore, denying the doctrine of Eutyches, lift up our voice, along with the Universal Church, whereof that woman was a figure, let us lift up our heart as well as our voice from the company, and say unto the Saviour: Blessed is the womb that bare thee, and the paps which thou hast sucked. Blessed Mother, of whom one hath said thou art His Mother, Who reigns over earth and over heaven for ever.

content.latin: Quinímmo beáti qui áudiunt verbum Dei et custódiunt. Pulchre Salvátor attestatióni mulíeris ánnuit, non eam tantúmmodo quæ Verbum Dei corporáliter generáre merúerat, sed et omnes qui idem Verbum spiritáliter audítu fídei concípere, et boni óperis custódia vel in suo vel in proximórum corde párere et quasi álere studúerint, asséverans esse beátos; quia, et éadem Dei Génetrix, et inde quidem beáta quia Verbi incarnándi minístra facta est temporális, sed inde multo beátior quia eiúsdem semper amándi custos manébat ætérna.
content.english: Yea, rather, blessed are they that hear the Word of God and keep it. How nobly doth the Saviour say “Yea” to the woman's blessing, declaring also that not only is she blessed who was meet to give bodily birth to the Word of God, but that all they who spiritually conceive the same Word by the hearing of faith, and, by keeping it through good works, bring it forth and, as it were, carefully nurse it, in their own hearts, and in the hearts of their neighbours, are also blessed. Yea, and that the very Mother of God herself was blessed in being for a while the handmaid of the Word of God made Flesh, but that she was much more blessed in this, that through her love she keepeth Him for ever.

content.english: May every heart be pure from sin

content.latin: Absístat et vecórdia;
content.english: And folly find no place therein:

content.latin: Carnis terat supérbiam
content.english: Scant need of food, excess denied,

content.latin: Potus cibíque párcitas.

content.latin: Ut, cum dies abscésserit,
content.english: That when the light of day is gone,

content.latin: Noctémque sors redúxerit,

content.latin: Mundi per abstinéntiam
content.english: We, free from cares the world affords,

content.english: All praise, Eternal Son, to thee:

content.latin: Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
content.english: All glory, as is ever meet,

content.english: To God the holy Paraclete.

content.english: Psalm 53 [1]

segments.t: Psalmus 53

content.latin: 53:3 Deus, in nómine tuo salvum me fac: * et in virtúte tua iúdica me.
content.english: 53:3 Save me, O God, by thy name, * and judge me in thy strength.

segments.t: Deus, in nómine tuo salvum me fac: * et in virtúte tua iúdica me.

content.latin: 53:4 Deus, exáudi oratiónem meam: * áuribus pércipe verba oris mei.
content.english: 53:4 O God, hear my prayer: * give ear to the words of my mouth.

segments.t: Deus, exáudi oratiónem meam: * áuribus pércipe verba oris mei.

content.latin: 53:5 Quóniam aliéni insurrexérunt advérsum me, et fortes quæsiérunt ánimam meam: * et non proposuérunt Deum ante conspéctum suum.
content.english: 53:5 For strangers have risen up against me; and the mighty have sought after my soul: * and they have not set God before their eyes.

segments.t: Quóniam aliéni insurrexérunt advérsum me, et fortes quæsiérunt ánimam meam: * et non proposuérunt Deum ante conspéctum suum.

content.latin: 53:6 Ecce enim, Deus ádiuvat me: * et Dóminus suscéptor est ánimæ meæ.
content.english: 53:6 For behold God is my helper: * and the Lord is the protector of my soul.

segments.t: Ecce enim, Deus ádiuvat me: * et Dóminus suscéptor est ánimæ meæ.

content.latin: 53:7 Avérte mala inimícis meis: * et in veritáte tua dispérde illos.
content.english: 53:7 Turn back the evils upon my enemies; * and cut them off in thy truth.

segments.t: Avérte mala inimícis meis: * et in veritáte tua dispérde illos.

content.latin: 53:8 Voluntárie sacrificábo tibi, * et confitébor nómini tuo, Dómine: quóniam bonum est:
content.english: 53:8 I will freely sacrifice to thee, * and will give praise, O God, to thy name: because it is good:

segments.t: Voluntárie sacrificábo tibi, * et confitébor nómini tuo, Dómine: quóniam bonum est:

content.latin: 53:9 Quóniam ex omni tribulatióne eripuísti me: * et super inimícos meos despéxit óculus meus.
content.english: 53:9 For thou hast delivered me out of all trouble: * and my eye hath looked down upon my enemies.

segments.t: Quóniam ex omni tribulatióne eripuísti me: * et super inimícos meos despéxit óculus meus.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
Psalmus 118(1-16)

content.latin: 118:1 (Aleph) Beáti immaculáti in via: * qui ámbulant in lege Dómini.
content.english: 118:1 (Aleph) Blessed are the undefiled in the way, * who walk in the law of the Lord.

segments.t: 118:1 (Aleph)
Beáti immaculáti in via: * qui ámbulant in lege Dómini.

content.latin: 118:2 Beáti, qui scrutántur testimónia eius: * in toto corde exquírunt eum.
content.english: 118:2 Blessed are they that search his testimonies: * that seek him with their whole heart.

segments.t: Beáti, qui scrutántur testimónia eius: * in toto corde exquírunt eum.

content.latin: 118:3 Non enim qui operántur iniquitátem, * in viis eius ambulavérunt.
content.english: 118:3 For they that work iniquity, * have not walked in his ways.

segments.t: Non enim qui operántur iniquitátem, * in viis eius ambulavérunt.

content.latin: 118:4 Tu mandásti * mandáta tua custodíri nimis.
content.english: 118:4 Thou hast commanded * thy commandments to be kept most diligently.

segments.t: Tu mandásti * mandáta tua custodíri nimis.

content.latin: 118:5 Útinam dirigántur viæ meæ, * ad custodiéndas iustificatiónes tuas!
content.english: 118:5 O! that my ways may be directed * to keep thy justifications.

segments.t: Útinam dirigántur viæ meæ, * ad custodiéndas iustificatiónes tuas!

content.latin: 118:6 Tunc non confúndar, * cum perspéxero in ómnibus mandátis tuis.
content.english: 118:6 Then shall I not be confounded, * when I shall look into all thy commandments.

segments.t: Tunc non confúndar, * cum perspéxero in ómnibus mandátis tuis.

content.latin: 118:7 Confitébor tibi in directióne cordis: * in eo quod dídici iudícia iustítiæ tuæ.
content.english: 118:7 I will praise thee with uprightness of heart, * when I shall have learned the judgments of thy justice.

segments.t: Confitébor tibi in directióne cordis: * in eo quod dídici iudícia iustítiæ tuæ.

content.latin: 118:8 Iustificatiónes tuas custódiam: * non me derelínquas usquequáque.
content.english: 118:8 I will keep thy justifications: * O! do not thou utterly forsake me.

segments.t: Iustificatiónes tuas custódiam: * non me derelínquas usquequáque.

content.latin: 118:9 (Beth) In quo córrigit adolescéntior viam suam? * In custodiéndo sermónes tuos.
content.english: 118:9 (Béth) By what doth a young man correct his way? * By observing thy words.

segments.t: In quo córrigit adolescéntior viam suam? * In custodiéndo sermónes tuos.

content.latin: 118:10 In toto corde meo exquisívi te: * ne repéllas me a mandátis tuis.
content.english: 118:10 With my whole heart have I sought after thee: * let me not stray from thy commandments.

segments.t: In toto corde meo exquisívi te: * ne repéllas me a mandátis tuis.

content.latin: 118:11 In corde meo abscóndi elóquia tua: * ut non peccem tibi.
content.english: 118:11 Thy words have I hidden in my heart, * that I may not sin against thee.

segments.t: In corde meo abscóndi elóquia tua: * ut non peccem tibi.

content.latin: 118:12 Benedíctus es, Dómine: * doce me iustificatiónes tuas.
content.english: 118:12 Blessed art thou, O Lord: * teach me thy justifications.

segments.t: Benedíctus es, Dómine: * doce me iustificatiónes tuas.

content.latin: 118:13 In lábiis meis, * pronuntiávi ómnia iudícia oris tui.
content.english: 118:13 With my lips * I have pronounced all the judgments of thy mouth.

segments.t: In lábiis meis, * pronuntiávi ómnia iudícia oris tui.

content.latin: 118:14 In via testimoniórum tuórum delectátus sum, * sicut in ómnibus divítiis.
content.english: 118:14 I have been delighted in the way of thy testimonies, * as in all riches.

segments.t: In via testimoniórum tuórum delectátus sum, * sicut in ómnibus divítiis.

content.latin: 118:15 In mandátis tuis exercébor: * et considerábo vias tuas.
content.english: 118:15 I will meditate on thy commandments: * and I will consider thy ways.

segments.t: In mandátis tuis exercébor: * et considerábo vias tuas.

content.latin: 118:16 In iustificatiónibus tuis meditábor: * non oblivíscar sermónes tuos.
content.english: 118:16 I will think of thy justifications: * I will not forget thy words.

segments.t: In iustificatiónibus tuis meditábor: * non oblivíscar sermónes tuos.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
Psalmus 118(17-32)

content.latin: 118:17 (Ghimel) Retríbue servo tuo, vivífica me: * et custódiam sermónes tuos:
content.english: 118:17 (Ghimel) Give bountifully to thy servant, enliven me * and I shall keep thy words.

segments.t: 118:17 (Ghimel)
Retríbue servo tuo, vivífica me: * et custódiam sermónes tuos:

content.latin: 118:18 Revéla óculos meos: * et considerábo mirabília de lege tua.
content.english: 118:18 Open thou my eyes: * and I will consider the wondrous things of thy law.

segments.t: Revéla óculos meos: * et considerábo mirabília de lege tua.

content.latin: 118:19 Íncola ego sum in terra: * non abscóndas a me mandáta tua.
content.english: 118:19 I am a sojourner on the earth: * hide not thy commandments from me.

segments.t: Íncola ego sum in terra: * non abscóndas a me mandáta tua.

content.latin: 118:20 Concupívit ánima mea desideráre iustificatiónes tuas, * in omni témpore.
content.english: 118:20 My soul hath coveted to long for thy justifications, * at all times.

segments.t: Concupívit ánima mea desideráre iustificatiónes tuas, * in omni témpore.

content.latin: 118:21 Increpásti supérbos: * maledícti qui declínant a mandátis tuis.
content.english: 118:21 Thou hast rebuked the proud: * they are cursed who decline from thy commandments.

segments.t: Increpásti supérbos: * maledícti qui declínant a mandátis tuis.

content.latin: 118:22 Aufer a me oppróbrium, et contémptum: * quia testimónia tua exquisívi.
content.english: 118:22 Remove from me reproach and contempt: * because I have sought after thy testimonies.

segments.t: Aufer a me oppróbrium, et contémptum: * quia testimónia tua exquisívi.

content.latin: 118:23 Étenim sedérunt príncipes, et advérsum me loquebántur: * servus autem tuus exercebátur in iustificatiónibus tuis.
content.english: 118:23 For princes sat, and spoke against me: * but thy servant was employed in thy justifications.

segments.t: Étenim sedérunt príncipes, et advérsum me loquebántur: * servus autem tuus exercebátur in iustificatiónibus tuis.

content.latin: 118:24 Nam et testimónia tua meditátio mea est: * et consílium meum iustificatiónes tuæ.
content.english: 118:24 For thy testimonies are my meditation: * and thy justifications my counsel.

segments.t: Nam et testimónia tua meditátio mea est: * et consílium meum iustificatiónes tuæ.

content.latin: 118:25 (Daleth) Adhǽsit paviménto ánima mea: * vivífica me secúndum verbum tuum.
content.english: 118:25 (Daleth) My soul hath cleaved to the pavement: * quicken thou me according to thy word.

segments.t: 118:25 (Daleth)
Adhǽsit paviménto ánima mea: * vivífica me secúndum verbum tuum.

content.latin: 118:26 Vias meas enuntiávi, et exaudísti me: * doce me iustificatiónes tuas.
content.english: 118:26 I have declared my ways, and thou hast heard me: * teach me thy justifications.

segments.t: Vias meas enuntiávi, et exaudísti me: * doce me iustificatiónes tuas.

content.latin: 118:27 Viam iustificatiónum tuárum ínstrue me: * et exercébor in mirabílibus tuis.
content.english: 118:27 Make me to understand the way of thy justifications: * and I shall be exercised in thy wondrous works.

segments.t: Viam iustificatiónum tuárum ínstrue me: * et exercébor in mirabílibus tuis.

content.latin: 118:28 Dormitávit ánima mea præ tǽdio: * confírma me in verbis tuis.
content.english: 118:28 My soul hath slumbered through heaviness: * strengthen thou me in thy words.

segments.t: Dormitávit ánima mea præ tǽdio: * confírma me in verbis tuis.

content.latin: 118:29 Viam iniquitátis ámove a me: * et de lege tua miserére mei.
content.english: 118:29 Remove from me the way of iniquity: * and out of thy law have mercy on me.

segments.t: Viam iniquitátis ámove a me: * et de lege tua miserére mei.

content.latin: 118:30 Viam veritátis elégi: * iudícia tua non sum oblítus.
content.english: 118:30 I have chosen the way of truth: * thy judgments I have not forgotten.

segments.t: Viam veritátis elégi: * iudícia tua non sum oblítus.

content.latin: 118:31 Adhǽsi testimóniis tuis, Dómine: * noli me confúndere.
content.english: 118:31 I have stuck to thy testimonies, O Lord: * put me not to shame.

segments.t: Adhǽsi testimóniis tuis, Dómine: * noli me confúndere.

content.latin: 118:32 Viam mandatórum tuórum cucúrri, * cum dilatásti cor meum.
content.english: 118:32 I have run the way of thy commandments, * when thou didst enlarge my heart.

segments.t: Viam mandatórum tuórum cucúrri, * cum dilatásti cor meum.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

Allelúia, confitémini Dómino, quóniam in sǽculum misericórdia eius, allelúia, allelúia.

content.latin: Regi sæculórum immortáli et invisíbili, soli Deo honor et glória in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: Now to the king of ages, immortal, invisible, the only God, be honour and glory for ever and ever. Amen.

content.english: ℣. Thou that wast born of the Virgin Mary.

content.english: ℟. Have mercy on us.

content.english: ℟. Christ, Son of the living God, * have mercy on us.

segments.t: Christe, Fili Dei vivi, * Miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℣. Exsúrge, Christe, ádiuva nos.
content.english: ℣. Arise, O Christ, and help us.

segments.t: Exsúrge, Christe, ádiuva nos.

content.latin: ℟. Et líbera nos propter nomen tuum.
content.english: ℟. And deliver us for thy name's sake.

segments.t: Et líbera nos propter nomen tuum.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

segments.t: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

segments.t: Et clamor meus ad te véniat.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Dómine Deus omnípotens, qui ad princípium huius diéi nos perveníre fecísti: tua nos hódie salva virtúte; ut in hac die ad nullum declinémus peccátum, sed semper ad tuam iustítiam faciéndam nostra procédant elóquia, dirigántur cogitatiónes et ópera.
content.english: O Lord, our heavenly Father, Almighty and everlasting God, who has safely brought us to the beginning of this day: defend us by thy mighty power; and grant that this day we fall into no sin, but that all our doings may be ordered by thy governance, to do always what is righteous in thy sight.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

segments.t: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

segments.t: Et clamor meus ad te véniat.

content.english: ℣. Let us bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedicámus Dómino.

content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: Tértio Idus Octóbris Luna secúnda Anno Dómini 2026
content.english: Of holy Edward, King of England, who died upon the 5th day of January, but whose feast is kept upon the 13th day of October, which is that of the translation of his body.

content.latin: Sancti Eduárdi, Regis Anglórum et Confessóris, qui Nonis Ianuárii obdormívit in Dómino, sed hac die, ob Translatiónem córporis eius, potíssimum cólitur.
content.english: October 13th 2026, the 2nd day of the Moon, were born into the better life:

content.latin: Apud Tróadem, Asiæ minóris urbem, natális sancti Carpi, qui fuit discípulus beáti Pauli Apóstoli.
content.english: At Troas, in Asia Minor, holy Carpus, the disciple of the blessed Apostle Paul.

content.latin: Córdubæ, in Hispánia, item natális sanctórum Mártyrum Fausti, Ianuárii et Martiális; qui, primo equúlei pœna cruciáti, deínde, supercíliis rasis, déntibus evúlsis, áuribus quoque et náribus præcísis, ignis passióne martýrium consummárunt.
content.english: At Cordova, in Spain, (in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian,) the holy martyrs Faustus, Januarius, and Martial, who were first racked, then had their eyebrows, ears, and noses cut off, and their teeth drawn, and at last completed their suffering martyrdom by fire.

content.latin: Thessalonícæ sancti Floréntii Mártyris, qui, post vária torménta, igne combústus est.
content.english: At Thessalonica, the holy martyr Florence, who was put to diverse tortures and then burnt.

content.latin: Apud Stokeráviam, in Austria, sancti Colmánni Mártyris.
content.english: In Austria, (in the eleventh century,) the holy martyr Colman.

content.latin: Antiochíæ sancti Theóphili Epíscopi, qui, sextus post beátum Petrum Apóstolum, eiúsdem Ecclésiæ Pontificátum ténuit.
content.english: At Ceuta, in Morocco, (in the year 1221,) seven holy martyrs belonging to the Order of Friars Minor namely, Daniel, Samuel, Angelo, Domnus, Leo, Nicolas, and Hugolin for their preaching of the Gospel and their confutation of the Mohammedan religion, the Saracens inflicted upon them insults, chains, and stripes, and then beheaded them and so they gained the palm of martyrdom.

content.latin: Turónis, in Gállia, sancti Venántii, Abbátis et Confessóris.
content.english: At Antioch, (towards the end of the second century,) the holy Patriarch Theophilus, the sixth after the blessed Apostle Peter, who held the bishopric of that church.

content.latin: Apud Sublácum, in Látio, sanctæ Chelidóniæ Vírginis.
content.english: At Tours, (in the fifth century,) the holy Confessor Venantius, Abbot (of St. Martin's Monastery.)

content.latin: ℣. Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
content.english: At Subiaco, in Latium, the holy Virgin Chelidonia.

segments.t: Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℣. And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: ℣. Pretiósa in conspéctu Dómini.
content.english: ℣. Precious in the sight of the Lord

segments.t: Pretiósa in conspéctu Dómini.

content.latin: ℟. Mors Sanctórum eius.
content.english: ℟. Is the death of his saints.

segments.t: Mors Sanctórum eius.

content.latin: Sancta María et omnes Sancti intercédant pro nobis ad Dóminum, ut nos mereámur ab eo adiuvári et salvári, qui vivit et regnat in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Holy Mary and all the Saints, intercede for us with the Lord, our God, so that we may merit His help and salvation, who lives and reigns for ever and ever.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.english: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

segments.t: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

segments.t: Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

segments.t: Sed líbera nos a malo.

content.latin: ℣. Réspice in servos tuos, Dómine, et in ópera tua, et dírige fílios eórum.
content.english: ℣. Look upon thy servants and upon thy works: and direct their children.

segments.t: Réspice in servos tuos, Dómine, et in ópera tua, et dírige fílios eórum.

content.latin: ℟. Et sit splendor Dómini Dei nostri super nos, et ópera mánuum nostrárum dírige super nos, et opus mánuum nostrárum dírige.
content.english: ℟. And let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us. Direct thou the works of our hands; yea, the work of our hands do thou direct.

segments.t: Et sit splendor Dómini Dei nostri super nos, et ópera mánuum nostrárum dírige super nos, et opus mánuum nostrárum dírige.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Dirígere et sanctificáre, régere et gubernáre dignáre, Dómine Deus, Rex cæli et terræ, hódie corda et córpora nostra, sensus, sermónes et actus nostros in lege tua, et in opéribus mandatórum tuórum: ut hic et in ætérnum, te auxiliánte, salvi et líberi esse mereámur, Salvátor mundi: Qui vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: O Lord, Almighty God, King of heaven and earth, Saviour of the world, bless, lead, rule and govern our hearts and bodies, our senses, words and deeds today, following thy law and commandments, that here and for eternity with thy help we shall be saved in freedom. Who livest and reignest, world without end.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.english: Benediction. May Almighty God arrange our deeds and our day in His peace.

Dies et actus nostros in sua pace dispónat Dóminus omnípotens.

content.english: And the Lord direct your hearts, in the charity of God, and the patience of Christ.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.english: Benediction. May the Lord bless us, ✠ protect us from all evil and bring us to everlasting life. And may the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.

segments.t: Benedictio.

content.english: Art with the Father and the Son,
